alex: Quick update from the spec-decode contrastive holdout run we landed on this morning. Ran 12k holdout prompts (mix of instr/QA/code) across three configs: baseline greedy, speculative-contrastive (our new sketch), and speculative-two-stage.

Results (p50 latency / tokens/sec / QA-F1 delta vs baseline):
- baseline (greedy, 8-bit): 120ms p50 / 1.0x / +0.0 F1
- speculative-contrastive (4-bit quant candidate): 86ms p50 (-28%) / 1.9x / -0.6 F1
- speculative-two-stage (4-bit): 78ms p50 (-35%) / 2.1x / -1.8 F1

Notes: contrastive holds up much better on instruction prompts; two-stage is fastest but shows a bigger hit on exact-match QA and code completion tests. Tradeoff looks promising because contrastive keeps most of the quality while giving a substantial perf boost.

Command we used to run the harness (for reproducibility):
```
./rbench run --dataset holdout_v2.csv --model /models/llama3-70b-q4 --speculative sampler=contrastive,k=4,confirm_thresh=0.55 --batch 8 --save results/contrastive.json
```

priya: nice. what's the holdout split? how many of the prompts had long prefix contexts (>512 tokens)?

alex: holdout_v2 is 12k total: 40% instr, 30% QA, 20% code, 10% chit-chat. ~18% had >512 token prefixes, we tracked that as a separate slice. Contrastive actually did slightly better on long-prefix slices vs two-stage (p50 95ms vs 110ms).

michael: curious about quant interaction — both spec runs were q4, right? did you try speculative-contrastive with q8 to isolate quantization effect vs decoding algorithm?

alex: yes both q4. We ran an extra q8 contrastive run on a 2k subset: latency was 100ms p50 (vs 86ms q4) and F1 delta was -0.3 (vs -0.6 q4). So roughly ~0.3 F1 hit from q4 quantization on top of decoding changes.

sarah: for production rollout, what's your recommended A/B threshold for auto-fallback? our SLO is <120ms p50 and <=1.0 F1 delta on key QA set. contrastive meets latency but is close on F1.

alex: propose phased canary: 10% traffic -> measure per-route QA-F1 over 24h and abort if any route drops >1.0. fallback policy: route to baseline greedy for that route id for 1h. plan to enable model-level confirm_thresh tuning per-route.

jin: can you drop the per-prompt CSV and the code completion diffs? want to run my own microbench.

alex: uploaded results to s3: s3://redwood-evals/2009876543/contrastive_results.tar.gz (contains per-prompt csvs, diffs, and sample failures).

eval-bot: Eval harness finished: processed=12000, failures=4, avg_token_latency=12.3ms, artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/2009876543/contrastive_results.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

priya: can we add a small adversarial prompt set (edge-tokenization cases) before canary? my worry is subtle tokenization/non-determinism causing silent regressions.

alex: agree. adding adversarial_lex.csv (2k prompts) to the canary gate. also increasing confirm_thresh to 0.6 for code-heavy routes as a safeguard.

michael: for the quant story — let's do a micro-run with mixed q4/q8 routing (cheap path q4 for non-critical routes) in the Dedicated pool. helps understand tail and memory pressure.

alex: good call. I'll spin a dedicated job next week and post results. For now, next steps: 1) add adversarial set to canary, 2) run mixed q routing micro-canary, 3) define per-route confirm_thresh defaults and fallout thresholds.

sarah: sounds good. please @channel when the canary is live. :rocket:

alex: will do. thanks all.
